the synthesis, characterization, anticancer activity, and molecular modelling studies of novel benzothiazoles.
the synthesis and biological evaluation of some new 2-pheny-1,3- benzothiazole derivatives.
the synthesis, anticancer activity, and docking of some novel 2-arylbenzothiazoles as EGFR inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 4'-metyl substituted compounds were the most active compounds against MCF- 7 cells.
the compounds with 4'-methoxy substitution at the 2- phenyl moiety showed the highest activity against the breast cancer cell line.

the compounds 2-(2,4'-dimethoxy phenyl)-4-fluoro-5-methyl benzothiazole (3a) and 2-(2'-methyl phenyl)-4'-methoxy-5-methyl-5'-nitro-2H benzothiazole-3-carboxaldehyde (5b) showed the best anti-breast cancer activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the compounds with 4' methyl and fluoro substitutions at 4 position of the 2 phenyl group of the benzothiazoles were found to be the most active.
the 2-Phenyl-1, 3-benzothizoles are a promising class of tyrosine kinase inhibitor with the potential to be developed as anticancer agents.
the 3-Cl-2-Ph-BT and 3-F-2-Ph- BT were the best compounds for the EGFR inhibition and they were also the most active compounds in the MCF-7 cell line.
The main takeaway from our work is that
2-phenylethyl substituted benzothiazole is the best template for the synthesis of anticancer compounds.
the 4'-substituted compounds are more potent inhibitors of EGFR than the 3'-substituted derivatives.
the 2,4-difluoro-1,3 benzothiazoles with the 4'-methylene and 4'-methoxy substitution at 2-Phenyl moiety showed good anticancer activity against breast cancer cell line MCF-7.
